newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish bond futures ended 50 basis points higher on Monday amid expectations that the Bank of Spain may tomorrow cut rates for the third time this year.
"Not only does the market think they will cut rates by 25 basis points. It expects the the repo rate to be pushed down to 5.25 percent in a couple of months," a dealer in Madrid said.

A Reuter poll earlier this morning showed ten out of eleven financial experts were expecting a 25 bps cut in the 5.75 percent key money market rate. A stronger peseta, after a tamed March CPI, supported this view.
But dealers said at the longer end bonds will soon find a ceiling, and few traders said they would be surprised if the market fell after tomorrow's expected easing.
"I expect the future contract to be rangebound between 114 at most and 111," he said, adding that the market is looking for the right time to consolidate.
The 10-year spread over Bunds ended down at 92 basis points from 96 bps this morning.
"Such a spread is too high. Bonos are offering more value at the shorter end," a dealer added.
